annotations: West Virginia's Eastern Panhandle, 261 ways. Unposted rural county roads (tertiary and unclassified) that beta rates LTS 4 on the 50 mph rural default, re-rated on WVDOT's 2020 counts as the owner chose: under 500 a day with a count station on the route, LTS 3; 500 to 1,500 a day, or no count station within 2 km, LTS 3.5. Counts read 10% high for 2020. Left at the formula: county roads over 1,500 a day; secondary and primary roads and links; any way with a posted limit; roads inside the Census urban areas, which the remade urban-roads list re-rates (except seven busy county roads kept at LTS 4, and one piece of North Fairfax Boulevard kept at LTS 2).

rows.reason: The owner, 2026-10-30, asked for West Virginia's ratings to be calibrated like DC's, Maryland's and Virginia's ("Since we also have it, also calibrate west virginia too"). West Virginia has no agency stress layer, so its roads are rated by the formula alone, with no traffic count, and an unposted rural county road is read at the 50 mph rural default (LTS 4) however few cars use it. Shown WVDOT's 2020 traffic counts and Maryland SHA's ratings of comparable roads (rural, no shoulder, 40-45 mph: SHA LTS 3 on about 60-67% of miles under 1,500 a day), he chose on 2026-10-30 "Filtered counts, 3 and 3.5": real counts only on county roads; under 500 a day goes from 4 to 3; 500 to 1,500 a day, or no count station, goes to 3.5.
